A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-Mirage benchmark and Grounded Self-Distillation research, despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, adaptation results, loss ablations, and training-duration experiments in Tables 1–2 and Appendix Tables A–C.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and adaptation results, external-dataset evaluations, metric controls, and backbone-transfer experiments in Tables 1–5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The dual-view LoRA pipeline, plane mixture, and HKR/NKP losses remain. Section 4.3 revises the reported objective: the null expert and optional entropy term disappear, negative images receive preservation-only training, and the background mask excludes the entire adjacent ring. Appendix I adds backbone-specific adapter placements for ZoeDepth and Marigold. These refine and extend the retained method.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluation on 3D-Visual-Illusion, KITTI15, and Depth-in-the-Wild, substantially extending external illusion and general-depth coverage. Appendix B adds matched non-illusory and Gaussian-perturbed test scenarios. The original 468-scene benchmark and Penn-Fudan/CamVid training data remain; DA-2K evaluation already appeared in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains its foundation-model comparator roster. V2's new 3DVI comparison includes additional methods such as Metric3D, DUSt3R, VGGT, RAFT-Stereo, Selective-RAFT, and 3DVI. Table 5 adds Simple L1 adaptation and decoder finetuning; encoder finetuning was already evaluated in v1. These substantially broaden the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The stated crop requirement changes from retaining at least 40% of the ROI diagonal to the ROI occupying at least 40% of crop area. DCS/CCS aggregation is revised, and v2 adds standard depth metrics and globally affine-aligned 3DVI evaluation. Appendix Table A changes the duration study from epochs 1/2/4/6 to 1/2/3/4. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a four-scene, sixteen-crop illusion-removal/noise control, loss-weight sensitivity tests, backbone-transfer analyses, simpler adaptation ablations, and a curved-surface case study. The original loss-removal tests remain, but v1's separate epoch trajectories for each removed loss and its extended-training visualization are removed. The questions tested and supporting analyses change substantially.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its experiments. Additional epochs, model variants, and control conditions do not introduce repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the proposed method's DCS/CCS from 64.20/2.036e-4 to 58.64/1.907e-4, and ZoeDepth's from 467.7/1.001e-3 to 589.3/1.505e-3. Ablation and duration results are revised, and extensive external-dataset, control, and transfer results are added. Because definitions and settings also change, these updated scores do not establish a same-setting improvement between versions.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 substantively revises the mathematical definitions. V1 defines per-instance scores using ROI sums and per-pixel averages; v2 defines DCS through the norm of the dataset centroid and average instance norms, and CCS through corresponding off-diagonal projections. The formal carrier assumption also broadens from physically planar to locally low-curvature or piecewise-smooth. These are more than notation changes.

C1.justification: The benchmark–metrics–mitigation contribution structure remains. V2 narrows benchmark novelty from the first real-world illusion benchmark to the combination of paired context variation and complex ROI annotation, while broadening the stated target from planar to planar/low-curvature surfaces. These qualify the retained central claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly presents DCS/CCS as reference-free structural probes that complement ground-truth metrics and cannot guarantee metric-depth accuracy. It expands the explanation of piecewise-surface grounding, qualifies model-capacity interpretations, and acknowledges that genuine road hazards remain untested. The earlier untested-diffusion limitation becomes a qualified transfer-feasibility finding. These materially sharpen applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the source-image-level 90/10 split, scene and pair counts, three-pixel ring and one-pixel guard construction, and backbone-specific adaptation details. It supplies code and dataset addresses where v1 promised future release. The split is newly disclosed, not demonstrably newly introduced. A reporting inconsistency remains: the main text gives a 1.2% trainable fraction while Appendix J retains 0.7%.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds substantive positioning against Yao et al.'s 3D Visual Illusion work and Booster, distinguishing monocular context sensitivity from binocular fusion and reflective-surface challenges. This supports the narrowed novelty claim. Additional stereo, multi-view, and metric-depth references accompany actual comparisons, substantially expanding the relevant research context.

P1.justification: Beyond changing the title, v2 systematically revises terminology, rewrites the metric and loss explanations, replaces the formal desired-objective presentation with conceptual properties, and condenses the original ablation narrative. The appendix is reorganized around implementation, controls, transfer, and safety. These constitute substantial explanatory and structural editing.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation and redraws the pipeline to show teacher supervision and local-plane fitting in both branches. It adds annotation, curvature, transfer, boundary, and control illustrations; merges the two qualitative loss-ablation figures; and restructures the tables. Most older appendix images are retained and relocated, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: V1 primarily validates mitigation through its own structural scores and limited preservation checks. V2 adds external ground-truth 3DVI evaluation, broader standard-depth checks, targeted metric controls, and transfer experiments, substantially strengthening validation. Explicit scene-level splitting and boundary implementation details improve reproducibility, while the revised pipeline figure better matches the method description. Some detailed training analyses are lost and reporting inconsistencies remain, but the gains clearly outweigh these limitations.
